company.text: Builders FirstSource is the largest US supplier of building products, prefabricated components and value-added services to professional homebuilders, sub-contractors, remodelers and consumers, with about **575 locations in 43 states**. Products include factory-built roof and floor trusses, wall panels, stairs, windows, doors, millwork and lumber, plus **digital solutions** for homebuilders. CEO: **Peter Jackson**. In Q3 2026 net sales were **$3.9B (−2.2%)** due to weaker housing starts, and the company is pushing productivity savings and investment in technology.

financials.text: **Q3 2026 (reported Oct 29, 2026):** net sales $3.9B (−2.2%); net income $60.4M ($0.56/share vs $1.10); adjusted EBITDA $311.1M (−28.3%, 8.1% margin). **FY2026 guidance:** net sales $14.2–14.6B; adjusted EBITDA $1.075–1.125B; free cash flow ~$400–450M. Productivity savings ~$57M YTD, $60–70M targeted for 2026. Employee count to be confirmed.

industry.text: Builders' suppliers are cutting costs in 2026. IT spend goes to things that cut support time or extend device life.

industry.title: Hybrid and mobile users
industry.text: Branches, truss plants, yards and field sales reps all need dependable docking, charging and carrying gear — not just desk setups.

talking_points: Sorry for the delay on the catalog — here it is. Which user groups are hardest to equip today: office, branch/yard, or field sales?
What do you standardize on now for **docks and hubs**? Any pain with mixed laptop brands or USB-C?
How do you buy peripherals — direct, through a reseller like CDW/Insight, or via the laptop vendor?
Would **sample units for one branch** be a useful test?
Who else weighs in on accessory standards — procurement, or your IT asset team?
